unit: WF5 Build Daily Digest conflict-notice sections and budget omission

source_qa_workflow.name: QA - WF5 Conflict Notice Digest Sections

description: A register large enough to exceed the 3600 character message ceiling, forcing the omission machinery to drop the lowest-priority sections while priority 0 survives.
why_it_exists: Conflict notices written by the WF5 conflict detector could be silently lost: a notice whose Telegram delivery failed or was abandoned never resurfaced anywhere the owner reads. The digest gained three notice sections plus an unreported-count headline, and this fixture set pins the status lifecycle (blank/PENDING/FAILED/EXHAUSTED/SENT) so a reported notice stays silent and an unreported one never does. This scenario additionally guards Fix 2: before it, sections dropped for the 3600 character Telegram budget vanished with no trace, so the owner could not tell that anything had been withheld.

input.scenario_name: Large dataset that exercises the 3600 character budget

assertions: diagnostics.reconciles is true: accounted actions equal distinct action ids
the rendered reply contains the section heading "CONFLICT NOTICES NEVER REPORTED"
already-reported notice CK-BIG-SENT never appears in the reply text
the reply contains "Conflict notices not yet reported to you: 3"
sections_omitted > 0: budget pressure genuinely occurred at this fixture size
the reply prints "OMITTED TO FIT ONE MESSAGE (<n>)" with the omitted count
every omitted section is named in the reply with "[priority P, N row(s), BUDGET_EXCEEDED, lowest priority dropped first]"
no priority 0 section (DATA_INTEGRITY_CONFLICT, TEST AND QA MATTERS, CONFLICT NOTICES NEVER REPORTED) is ever omitted
after omission the reply length is <= the 3600 character ceiling (budget_holds is true)
